sections.title: Why Nobody Listens To You (and how to fix it)

items.a: **professional keynotes sell a 1-hour *experience***: 30% education, 30% entertainment, 30% inspiration (energy transfer via voice), 10% X-factor (what makes you you). Over-indexing on any single pillar fails (pure education = sleep; pure magic = confusion; pure inspiration = nauseating).

items.q: What should you remember about **Virtual energy tax**?
items.a: **speaking to a camera drops natural energy 50–70%; amp** up deliberately for live Zoom and content. Monotone body → monotone voice; turn camera on to force movement.

items.q: What should you remember about **Eye contact on Zoom**?
items.a: **look at the camera, not yourself; Plexi** Cam trick centers webcam on screen for natural eye contact while seeing the other person.

items.q: What should you remember about **Play vs use**?
items.a: **influential moments require playing volume, melody, emotion, tonality, and** pause; most people only "use" their voice and wonder why they're ignored. Fear of judgment blocks play at the edges.

items.q: What should you remember about **Inner child unlock**?
items.a: **adults forgot play; reconnecting makes you** a magnet. "There's no such thing as adults — we're all big kids.".

items.q: What should you remember about **Perfection trap**?
items.a: **goal of perfection guarantees nerves; reframe** to "add maximum value." Self-consciousness = consciousness on self; redirect to serving the audience.

items.q: What should you remember about **Theater mistake rule**?
items.a: **if you don't make a big** deal out of an error, they won't; audience doesn't have your script.

items.q: What should you remember about **Exposure therapy**?
items.a: **nerves = insufficient reps; window cleaners desensitized over** 23 years; Vinh performed magic 1,000+ times. social exposure ladder: good morning → compliment → question over weeks/months.

items.q: What should you remember about **Be as big as the room**?
items.a: **too loud for intimate settings, too quiet** for large rooms; on camera, imagine 10–20 people and bring that energy; 1:1 dial down.

items.q: What should you remember about **Pre-speech routine**?
items.a: **3 cycles Wim Hof (12–15 min) → star jumps to** burn adrenaline → Hans Zimmer orchestral war music + personal funny-video folder for endorphins; 70s music at home as daily mood hack.

items.q: What should you remember about **High-status rapport**?
items.a: **pedestal = shrink and fanboy; humanize ("when they fart, it** still stinks"); mom's lesson — put the *lessons* on the pedestal, not the person. Storytelling beats feature lists for memorable CEO pitches.

items.q: What should you remember about **All the world's a stage**?
items.a: **Shakespeare frame; you play father, husband, teacher** roles daily; improving communication elevates every stage; luminary = actor + source of light.
